cards.text: Babylon just heard the LORD announce her downfall. Now He turns to His own people: 'Listen to this, O house of Jacob.' These are people from the line of Judah, who swear by the name of the LORD and call on the God of Israel.

cards.question: These people swear by the LORD's name and call on the God of Israel. But the LORD says something is missing. What is it?

cards.text: They even call themselves after the holy city and lean on the God of Israel, the LORD of Hosts. That's me in the junk drawer, telling the dead batteries next to me I'm a PROFESSIONAL stamper. From under a takeout menu.
Then the LORD reminds them that He foretold the former things long ago. They came straight out of His own mouth.

cards.question: The LORD foretold the former things long ago. What happened when He acted?
Why tell His people so far ahead? The LORD says, 'I knew that you are ___.'

cards.text: He paints the picture: 'your neck is iron and your forehead is bronze.' Friend, I lay flat in a drawer for YEARS and I was never THAT stiff.

cards.question: The LORD announced things to His stubborn people before they came to pass. What claim does He say that shuts down?

cards.text: They've heard it all, and the LORD asks if they won't acknowledge it. Then He turns the page.

cards.question: After the former things, what does the LORD say He'll tell His people from now on?
The LORD says these new things are created ___, and not long ago.

cards.text: So nobody can claim, 'I already knew them!' No 'yeah, I KNEW that' coworker energy allowed, friend.

cards.question: The LORD says His people's ears have been open for a long time.

cards.text: He knew how deceitful they are, and they've been called a rebel from birth. After THAT, I'm hiding under my chef's hat waiting for the oven door to slam.

cards.question: After calling out His deceitful, stubborn people, what does the LORD say He'll do with His wrath?
The LORD gives His reason: 'For the sake of My ___ I will delay My wrath.'

cards.text: He holds it back so they will not be cut off. Then He says, 'See, I have refined you, but not as silver.'

cards.question: The LORD refined His people, but not as silver. Where does He say He tested them?

answers.text: In the depths of the sea
In the dust of the desert

cards.text: I know ovens, friend, and this furnace is NOT baking cookies. Then the LORD says, 'For My own sake, My very own sake, I will act; for how can I let Myself be defamed?'

cards.question: The LORD says He will give His glory to another.

findings.problem: The opening card states a Bible fact from outside the passage, 'Babylon just heard the LORD announce her downfall' (Isaiah 47), with no reference. The card cites only Isaiah 48:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'They even call themselves...', 'That's me in the junk drawer...' and 'From under a takeout menu.' It isn't the opening card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new moment in his drawer backstory: him telling the dead batteries he's a professional stamper. The backstory says that in the drawer he gave up, didn't talk much and didn't joke at all. Jokes may make up small moments around his bakery, not new drawer history.

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: Nothing before this card points to stubbornness. Card 2 only says their worship lacks truth or righteousness. 'Fearful' and 'weary' are just as reasonable as reasons to tell people things far ahead, so picking 'stubborn' is mostly luck. A story card could set up the hard, unyielding picture first, or the question could change.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the exact next word of 'For the sake of My ___'. Reasoning from the passage points at least as strongly to 'people', since the wrath is delayed 'so that you will not be cut off.' The card tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
